Convert census tract aggregates to user-provided polygons using CNEFE points

Source: R/tracts_to_polygon.R
tracts_to_polygon.Rd

tracts_to_polygon() performs a dasymetric interpolation with the following steps:

  1. census tract totals are allocated to CNEFE dwelling points inside each tract;

  2. allocated values are aggregated to user-provided polygons (neighborhoods, administrative divisions, custom areas, etc.).

The function uses DuckDB with spatial extensions for the heavy work.

Unlike cnefe_counts() and compute_lumi(), this function does not expose a backend argument and relies on DuckDB exclusively. The dominant cost here is a spatial overlay between the full CNEFE point set of the municipality and the census tract polygons, which is a different workload from the tabular aggregation those other functions perform. Running that overlay in R would take prohibitively long in medium and large municipalities, so a pure-R fallback would offer users a path that does not finish rather than a slower one.

Usage

tracts_to_polygon(
  code_muni = NULL,
  polygon,
  year = 2022,
  vars = c("pop_ph", "pop_ch"),
  crs_output = NULL,
  scope = c("muni", "geom"),
  cache = TRUE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

code_muni

Numeric or character. One or more seven-digit IBGE municipality codes, for example 2927408 or c(2927408, 2919207). Repeated codes are dropped. With several codes, they're interpolated together, in a single allocation (see "Several municipalities").

Required under scope = "muni" (the default) and ignored under scope = "geom", which finds the municipalities that the polygons intersect (see "Municipalities detected from the polygons").

polygon

An sf::sf object with polygon geometries (POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON), in any CRS. Features with the same geometry as an earlier feature are dropped, with a message, and the first one is kept. Under scope = "muni", the diagnostics report the share of the allocated points of the municipalities in code_muni that falls inside the polygons. When polygons overlap, the diagnostics open with how many dwellings fall in more than one of them, since their allocated values are added to each.

year

Integer. The CNEFE data year. Currently only 2022 is supported. Defaults to 2022.

vars

Character vector. Names of tract-level variables to interpolate. Supported variables:

  • pop_ph: population in private households (Domicílios particulares).

  • pop_ch: population in collective households (Domicílios coletivos).

  • male: total male population.

  • female: total female population.

  • age_0_4, age_5_9, age_10_14, age_15_19, age_20_24, age_25_29, age_30_39, age_40_49, age_50_59, age_60_69, age_70m: population by age group.

  • race_branca, race_preta, race_amarela, race_parda, race_indigena: population by race/color (cor ou raça).

  • n_resp: number of household heads (Pessoas responsáveis por domicílios).

  • avg_inc_resp: average income of the household heads.

For a reference table mapping these variable names to the official IBGE census tract codes and descriptions, see tracts_variables_ref.

Allocation rules:

  • pop_ph is allocated only to private dwellings.

  • pop_ch is allocated only to collective dwellings.

  • n_resp is allocated only to private dwellings (same rule as pop_ph).

  • Demographic variables (male, female, age_*, race_*) are allocated to private dwellings when the tract has any; if the tract has zero private dwellings but has collective dwellings, they are allocated to collective.

  • avg_inc_resp is assigned (not split) to each private dwelling point; tracts with no private dwellings receive no allocation.

crs_output

The CRS for the output object. Default is NULL, which uses the original CRS of the polygon argument. Can be an EPSG code (e.g., 4326, 31983) or any CRS object accepted by sf::st_transform().

scope

Character. Which CNEFE addresses (and census tracts) the function works with. "muni" (the default, and the faster option) uses every address and tract of the municipalities in code_muni. "geom" uses the addresses that fall inside the polygons in polygon, whichever municipality they belong to, so the municipalities those polygons reach are read as well. See the section "Polygons at the edge of the region".

cache

Logical. If TRUE (default), the downloaded files are kept in the user cache directory and reused in later calls. These are the CNEFE file, the census tracts and the boundary of each municipality read. Only the tracts of those municipalities are downloaded, not the whole state. If FALSE, temporary files are used and deleted after the call. See clear_cache_muni(), clear_cache_tracts() and clear_cache_boundaries() to delete the cached files.

cache_dir

Character. Directory to use for cached downloads. If NULL (default), the CNEFETOOLS_CACHE_DIR environment variable is used when it is set, otherwise tools::R_user_dir() with which = "cache". Use this to point large downloads at a secondary drive or a shared volume.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print step messages and timing.

Value

An sf object with the user-provided polygons and the requested interpolated variables. The output CRS matches the original polygon CRS (or crs_output if specified).

Details

Several municipalities

Pass a vector of codes to interpolate a region that spans more than one municipality in a single call. The tracts and the CNEFE points of all of them go through one allocation, each point is matched only to the tracts of its own municipality, and the result has one row per polygon, whichever municipality the polygon crosses.

Calling the function once per municipality and binding the results isn't the same. A polygon that crosses a municipal border gets, in each call, only the part of the allocation that comes from the municipality of that call. Totals (every variable except avg_inc_resp) add up, so separate outputs can be combined by summing them by polygon. avg_inc_resp can't, because it's an average over the allocated points, and two averages don't give the average of the pooled points. Use a vector of codes instead.

Polygons at the edge of the region

Under the default scope = "muni", only the addresses and tracts of the municipalities in code_muni are used. A polygon that extends beyond them receives only the part of the allocation that comes from the municipalities requested, so its totals and avg_inc_resp describe a fraction of it. Use scope = "geom" for a complete result, which reads every municipality the polygons reach.

Municipalities detected from the polygons

With scope = "geom", the function finds the municipalities that the polygons intersect, using the 2022 IBGE municipal boundaries, and uses all of their tracts and addresses, even when they belong to different states. A message lists them, and a code_muni passed in this case is ignored.

Polygons from another source rarely follow the IBGE boundaries exactly, so a polygon along a municipal border can touch a neighboring municipality by a few meters. That neighbor is then downloaded and read too. The values are not affected, since only the points inside the polygons are aggregated, but use scope = "muni" with code_muni whenever you know which municipalities the polygons belong to, which is faster.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Interpolate population to user-provided polygons (neighborhoods of Lauro de Freitas-BA)
# Using geobr to download neighborhood boundaries
library(geobr)
nei_ldf <- subset(
  read_neighborhood(year = 2022),
  code_muni == 2919207
)
#> ℹ Using year/date 2022
poly_pop <- tracts_to_polygon(
  code_muni = 2919207,
  polygon = nei_ldf,
  vars = c("pop_ph", "pop_ch"),
  cache = FALSE
)
